Sand doesn't hold your fluid. It swallows it.
In permeable ground, every litre you pump in bleeds straight through the formation. Sand, gravel, broken rock. The bore face is full of tiny gaps and the fluid finds every one of them.

Pumping harder just feeds the problem. Thickening the mud loads the pump and still doesn't seal the wall.

The fix is forming a thin, tough layer right on the bore face. That layer blocks the gaps. Fluid stays in the hole. Pressure stays where you need it.

Once that seal is in place, you stop chasing your tank level and start making progress.
What ground type costs you the most fluid?

Filter Low seals the bore wall. That's the job.
It's a PAC polymer that builds a filter cake on the formation face. Once the cake is in place, your fluid stops bleeding into the ground.

Works in bentonite systems and polymer systems. It's in 6 Blick fluid programs across HDD, waterwell, and piling.

Dosage runs 0.5 to 2.5 kg per cubic metre in bentonite systems. 1.0 to 4.0 in polymer-only mixes. Start low and work up.

It controls fluid loss without thickening the whole system. If you need filtration and a clean-running fluid, that's what it's built for.

Tougher conditions or bigger bores? Give one of our team a call. We'll dial in the right program.
Losing fluid on a job right now? Phone the team.
